builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: MoARa: Module-Aware Rank Allocation and Structure-Preserving Decomposition for Low-Rank LLM Pre-training
summary: MoARa replaces uniform projection-rank allocation and raw-gradient projection in low-rank LLM pretraining methods such as GaLore with a static profiling-based per-module rank allocation plus block-wise magnitude-direction decomposition. It costs a one-time profiling pass, implementation complexity on top of an existing low-rank optimizer, and a reported 0.2% peak memory overhead under graph compilation. It can fail if the static rank profile does not transfer across architectures or training regimes, and its benefits are only realized during full pretraining runs at scales the reader does not perform.
rationale: The technique targets memory-efficient pretraining of 300M-7B models from scratch, which the reader's single 24 GB GPU, limited budget, and no-foundation-model-training constraint rule out, so it is worth tracking but not adopting.
technique: Module-aware rank allocation for low-rank pretraining

claims.statement: MoARa replaces uniform projection-rank allocation and raw-gradient projection in low-rank LLM pretraining methods such as GaLore with a static profiling-based per-module rank allocation plus block-wise magnitude-direction decomposition. It costs a one-time profiling pass, implementation complexity on top of an existing low-rank optimizer, and a reported 0.2% peak memory overhead under graph compilation. It can fail if the static rank profile does not transfer across architectures or training regimes, and its benefits are only realized during full pretraining runs at scales the reader does not perform.

GaLore with MoARa reaches standard GaLore's final perplexity in 37% fewer steps and 34% less wall-clock time on Llama 2 7B, with 0.2% peak reserved memory overhead; up to 41.7% step and 37.1% wall-clock reduction on compatible hosts.
